Subject: Help narrowing H100/A100/L4 split for Dedicated pilot

Hi Connor,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency headroom and the tracing. We're starting to map out a Dedicated pilot and need guidance on SKU selection. Our workload is a mix: 60% standard chat-style requests (~2k tokens roundtrip), 30% embeddings/rerank, and 10% long-context summarization (up to 80k tokens occasionally). Memory footprint for the long-context jobs spikes and we worry about eviction/tiling.

Questions:
- Do you recommend a single‑SKU Dedicated pool or a split (e.g., majority L4 with a memory‑heavy fallback)?
- If split, what nominal % should be reserved for H100/A100 vs L4?
- Any quick heuristics for when to pick A100 vs H100 (cost + memory vs perf)?

We're on a conservative procurement timeline but want an ops-safe plan that avoids OOMs during peak long-context windows. Hoping for a short matrix or rule‑of‑thumb we can include in the internal SOW.

Best,
Alice Jing
Head of AI Ops, Triton Labs

Subject: Re: Help narrowing H100/A100/L4 split for Dedicated pilot

Alice — thanks for the details, this is exactly the right time to lock heuristics in. Attached is a short matrix (triton_hw_fit_matrix.xlsx) and a quick pricing sketch. High level recommendations below; I'll add ops caveats after internal sync.

Quick summary (rule‑of‑thumb):
- Memory‑bound long‑context jobs (top 10% by token peak): assign to H100 80GB or A100 80GB pools. Use H100 when throughput sensitivity (generation QPS) is high and you need faster FP16 kernels; choose A100 if you prioritize memory headroom at slightly lower per‑GPU throughput but better cost per GB in some clouds.
- Latency‑sensitive chat/embeddings (majority): L4 burst pool is cost‑effective and has excellent token throughput for short contexts; pin to L4 when typical sequence length < 4k and model variant supports quantized kernels.
- Fallback/hedge: keep a small reserved H100 slot pool (~5‑10% of committed capacity) for warm KV‑cache restores and long‑tail OOMs. This reduces fallthroughing to on‑demand and avoids noisy neighbor retries.

Heuristic split (starting point for pilot):
- L4: 65% (chat + embeddings)
- A100/H100 memory pool: 30% (long‑context + heavy rerank) — start with A100 60/40 if cost sensitivity high
- Reserved H100 buffer: 5% (hot fallback)

Operational notes:
- KV cache locality matters: co‑locate long‑context producers with memory pool to reduce prefix transfer. If you use large prefix reuse, you get significant token cost savings via cache hits; we simulated expected token savings in kv_cache_latency_sim.csv.
- Tiling/OOM mitigation: prefer slot tiling (split large contexts across slots) over overly conservative SKU switching; tiling retains QoS and is supported by our runtime for both H100 and A100. L4 has smaller per‑instance memory and will OOM on 80k tokens without tiling.

I've kept the matrix conservative for procurement. Ben and Priyom — please review the attached sketch and add ops constraints or alternate splits if we think Triton should start H100‑heavy for their 80k tail.

Cheers,
Connor O'Brien
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Quick ops additions:
- Warmup strategy: for the pilot, schedule daily prober traffic to warm KV caches into the memory pool so the 80k windows don't incur cold transfer. That reduces burst demand by ~20–30% in our tests.
- Autoscaling policy: set static minimum for memory pool equal to expected concurrent long‑context jobs (not % of total). If they expect 3 simultaneous 80k jobs, reserve 3 slots; everything else can be dynamic.
- Billing visibility: make sure Triton's SRE accepts token‑level reporting for the long‑context tenants; otherwise they'll overcommit.

I ran the kv_cache_latency_sim.csv overnight — results look consistent with Connor's notes.

Ben Carter
Dedicated Ops, Redwood Inference

Procurement note for Triton:
- If Triton picks H100 for the memory pool we need to be explicit about the SLA and preemption behavior for the reserved buffer. H100 reserved slots should be part of the SOW with a price uplift (we propose +12% on base per‑GPU commit for H100 buffer).
- For A100 vs H100 choice: include a fallback clause in the contract to swap A100 -> H100 within 60 days if the long‑context tail proves more memory‑sensitive than predicted. That keeps the initial commit cost down but gives them an ops path.

I'm attaching a rough dedicated pricing sketch in the drive folder (dedicated‑pricing‑sketch.pdf). Connor — add any line items we should show as separate billable addons (e.g., cache warming, prober traffic).

Alice — attaching a consolidated pilot plan and the split I recommend based on your profile:
- Pilot commitment: 12 months, 40 reserved slots (initial billing commit)
  - L4 pool: 26 slots (65%) for chat/embeddings; quantized model variants where possible
  - A100 pool: 12 slots (30%) for long‑context; we selected A100 80GB to start to balance cost and memory; can swap to H100 if throughput tests require it
  - H100 buffer: 2 slots (5%) reserved for emergency warm fallthroughs
